Spatial kriging of SHmax axes after van den Boogaart & Schaeben (2002)

Source: R/interpolation_krige.R
stress2grid_kriging.Rd

Ordinary kriging of the doubled-angle embedding of SHmax axes, with a distance-only trace variogram (isotropy of measurements). The per-observation uncertainty, given as a standard deviation in degrees, is used as measurement error on the diagonal of the kriging matrix.

Usage

stress2grid_kriging(
  x,
  grid = NULL,
  lon_range = NULL,
  lat_range = NULL,
  gridsize = 2,
  R_range = 300,
  max_data = 50,
  min_data = 3L,
  min_dist_threshold = 200,
  vgm_model = c("spherical", "exponential", "gaussian"),
  nugget = 0,
  range_km = 300,
  use_uncertainty = TRUE,
  axial = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

sf object containing

azi

angles in degrees (e.g. orientation of \(\sigma_\text{Hmax}\))

unc

(optional) Uncertainties of azi in degree

type

(optional) Methods used for the determination of the direction of \(\sigma_\text{Hmax}\)

grid

(optional) Point object of class sf.

lon_range, lat_range

(optional) numeric vector specifying the minimum and maximum longitudes and latitudes (ignored if grid is specified).

gridsize

numeric. Target spacing of the regular grid in decimal degree. Default is 2.5. (is ignored if grid is specified)

R_range

numeric value or vector of search radii in km. Only observations within the radius are used.

max_data

integer. The number of nearest observations used for each prediction. Default is 50.

min_data

integer. If the number of observations within distance R_range is less than min_data, a missing value NA will be generated. Default is 3 for stress2grid() and 4 for stress2grid_stats().

min_dist_threshold

numeric. Distance threshold for smallest distance of the prediction location to the next observation location. Default is 200 km.

vgm_model

Variogram model: "spherical" (default), "exponential" or "gaussian". The sill is fixed at 1 (see details).

nugget

numeric in \([0, 1)\). Nugget of the trace variogram.

range_km

numeric. Range of the variogram model in km.

use_uncertainty

logical. If TRUE (default), unc (standard deviation in degrees) is used as measurement error.

axial

Must be TRUE. Only axial data are supported.

Value

sf object containing

lon,lat

longitude and latitude in degrees

azi

kriged axis direction in degrees (0 to 180), from the dominant eigenvector of the orientation tensor

sd

circular standard deviation of the axis in degrees, computed from conf as rad2deg(sqrt(-2 log(conf))) / 2

R

search radius in km

mdr

mean distance between grid point and data / R

N

number of observations used

conf

confidence in \([0, 1]\): length of the kriged doubled-angle vector, capped at 1. Equals \(2 \times \text{eig}_1 - 1\)

kvar

kriging variance on the trace-variogram scale

eig1

larger eigenvalue of the kriged orientation tensor, in \([0.5, 1]\). The smaller eigenvalue is 1 - eig1

Attribute "vgm" records the variogram parameters used.

Details

The method is the simplified ordinary-kriging form derived by van den Boogaart & Schaeben (2002) for axes in the embedding u u^T. Their isotropy-of-measurements assumption gives the trace variogram used here. The matrix-valued estimate is projected back onto the axes by taking the dominant eigenvector, which equals the direction of the predicted doubled-angle vector. The length of that vector is the confidence measure described in the paper.

Fit nugget and range_km to the empirical variogram from variogram_axial(). The variogram has sill 1, because the trace of the covariance of unit vectors is 1 (eq. 36 of the paper).

References

van den Boogaart, K.G. and Schaeben, H. (2002). Kriging of regionalized directions, axes, and orientations I. Mathematical Geology, 34(5), 479-503.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
data("san_andreas")
v <- variogram_axial(san_andreas)
res <- stress2grid_kriging(san_andreas, R_range = 300,
                           vgm_model = "spherical",
                           nugget = 0.1, range_km = 200)
head(res)
} # }
